owaspDescriptions.ASI01: Agent Goal Hijack: Manipulating agent goals via prompt injection, deceptive inputs, or poisoned data
owaspDescriptions.ASI02: Tool Misuse & Exploitation: Agents misusing legitimate tools through over-privileged access or unsafe delegation
owaspDescriptions.ASI03: Identity & Privilege Abuse: Exploiting delegation chains, credential inheritance, and privilege escalation in agents
owaspDescriptions.ASI04: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities: Compromised MCP tools, poisoned dependencies, and typosquatted agent components
owaspDescriptions.ASI05: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE): Shell injection, code hallucination, unsafe eval(), and sandbox escape via agents
owaspDescriptions.ASI06: Memory & Context Poisoning: RAG poisoning, shared context corruption, and long-term memory drift
owaspDescriptions.ASI07: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication: MITM on agent messages, protocol spoofing, and A2A registration attacks
owaspDescriptions.ASI08: Cascading Failures: Single faults propagating and amplifying across interconnected agents and workflows
owaspDescriptions.ASI09: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation: Social engineering via agent authority, fake explainability, and automation bias
owaspDescriptions.ASI10: Rogue Agents: Behavioral drift, goal deviation, self-replication, and emergent misalignment

hooks.name: Antigravity Review Modes
hooks.description: Agent execution modes: Request Review never auto-executes terminal commands except those on the Allow list; Always Proceed executes automatically except commands on the Deny list. Strict mode always prompts and ignores the allowlist entirely. A Security Preset controls whether all terminal commands and file accesses require review.
hooks.securityValue: The autonomy dial for Google's agent-first IDE, with an explicit paranoid setting: strict mode removes even the allowlist, so no accumulated convenience carve-outs survive into high-sensitivity work.
hooks.payload: mode: request-review | always-proceed; strict_mode ignores allowlist; Security Preset

hooks.name: Antigravity Terminal Allow/Deny Lists
hooks.description: Configurable command lists with regex support, e.g. command(git) or command(npm run (build|lint|test)). Allow list runs without prompting in Request Review mode; Deny list always prompts even in Always Proceed mode.
hooks.securityValue: Pattern-scoped command policy: safe scripts flow, everything else meets a human. Regex patterns deserve review discipline, since an over-broad pattern is a standing auto-approval.

hooks.name: Antigravity MCP Tool Allowlist
hooks.description: Per-project configuration of which MCP tools are available to the agent, preventing globally configured MCP servers from being exposed to every project.
hooks.securityValue: Project-scoped MCP least privilege: a personal MCP server configured globally does not silently become attack surface in a work repository.
hooks.payload: per-project allowed MCP tools (subset of global servers)

hooks.name: Antigravity Terminal Sandboxing
hooks.description: Kernel-level isolation for agent-executed terminal commands: a restricted environment with limited filesystem and network access.
hooks.securityValue: Containment beneath the permission layer: even an approved command runs with bounded filesystem and network reach.
